generator_metadata.summary: One to four colors each mark two diagonal corners of a rectangle. Draw every bounding-box border in first-reading-order color order; later borders overwrite earlier ones at overlaps. Native profiles include both diagonal orientations, overlapping boxes, and spans of eight or more.

## `ed55b2928ac3`

### Defect → repair

The previous source rejected lawful canonical examples, treated declared controls as aliases or ignored values, excluded boundary sizes, and silently tolerated unsupported/coercive overrides. Version 4.0.0 now validates all four canonical inputs, enforces exact keyed controls and bounds, rejects unknown/coercive overrides, and samples connected nonrectangular 3–6-cell shapes while preserving the canonical keyed transform.

### Parametric family

The default `plain` setting is the catalog program byte-for-byte. In `top_edge_to_8`, A clears the corner key, crops, and applies the key-selected transform; B reads the leftmost nonzero color on the transformed top row and recolors that color to 8. The retained wrong-order Racket program performs B on the untransformed crop and provably changes the selected query output.

sequential_dependency.intermediate: The combined reading-order outline grid produced from all sparse corner pairs.
sequential_dependency.step_a: Render every color-paired rectangle border in input reading order, allowing later borders to overwrite earlier overlap cells.
sequential_dependency.step_b: On that combined outline grid, recolor each zero cell that has nonzero support somewhere left, right, above, and below to 8.
sequential_dependency.why_b_depends_on_a: The sparse corner input contains no four-direction enclosure. Only A creates the border geometry that B tests, so applying B before A leaves those cells zero and changes the final output.

parametric_work.summary: Exact canonical outline default plus paint_enclosed sequential composition; matched inputs with overlap, both diagonals and long spans, four queries including 30×30 stress, protected replay, and wrong-order witness.
